conflicts.outcome: Persistence is a real constraint, so each count is computed from the same set its drill-down lists, for the signed-in organisation. Following DR1's judgement, a card whose state no service yet records waits (blockedBy) rather than shipping a count that is always zero. The fixed numbers are overruled. Every count also waits on the INS dashboard's requirements under Sam's 9 October rulings.

conflicts.about: What makes a real notification 'Action needed' when no real service records an 'Action required' status.

positions.says: The Action needed list holds notifications whose status is Action required, each carrying an error message such as 'ITAHC is missing'.
The page tells the trader to add missing information or upload documents to prevent the consignment being delayed.
After submitting, the real service tells the trader they still need to upload the health certificate and any other required documents.
The real service has no alerts, errors or messages anywhere; a rejected notification shows only on its status tag.
Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
How action-required is stored is the real team's decision.
The INS read model's part of the animals-dashboard rows is dropped, replacing c-149's 'carried into the INS read model'.

conflicts.outcome: Missing documents, as Design Release 2.1 works it out: a submitted notification still missing a required document (no ITAHC or health certificate attached), or with no animal identifier where one is required (one identifier is enough), counts as action needed, recorded by the animals backend as the 'Submitted action required' status. How that state is derived and stored is the real team's decision (Sam, 9 October). The animals frontend's own list shows it from the animals backend's record; the INS 'Action needed' count and drill-down, which list the signed-in organisation's such notifications with an 'Action required' tag and '<document> is missing' (or 'Information is missing'), wait on the INS dashboard's requirements, and how the state reaches the INS read model is settled when that area is re-distilled (9 October afternoon ruling). Authority-flagged actions are not part of this; they are added only when an outcome feed from the authorities exists.

The rest of the home is built to match Design Release 2.1. The link and count arrive with a later design that defines messages and a service that records them.

The already-blocked plants glance cards (inc-146) now also wait on the INS dashboard's requirements.

conflicts.outcome: The plants section's glance cards link like the live-animals and germinal-products ones: 'View tasks' to the Action needed drill-down showing only plants, 'View updates' to the Status updated drill-down showing only plants, and 'View requirements' to the Inspection required drill-down, so users can reach that page. The '#' links are DR2.1 placeholders for a cross-service flow the prototype cannot express, not a design to copy. The cards' counts, and the cards themselves, are built with the plants section once plants notifications reach the INS read model and the INS dashboard's requirements firm up (9 October afternoon ruling).

conflicts.about: Whether the service navigation keeps 'Log out', which DR2.1's navigation does not show.

positions.says: Authentication is a real constraint the prototype cannot express and overrides it.
The navigation reads Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account.
The fourth navigation item is 'Log out', linking to /auth/sign-out.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: signing out is authentication the prototype cannot express, so 'Log out' stays. The prototype claim is not overruled because it still backs the Templates item and the home having no back link.

conflicts.about: Which links a drill-down's notification card carries: DR2.1's fixed 'Copy as new' and 'View', or the status-driven links DR1 kept.

positions.says: inc-030 rejected: the dashboard card keeps its status-driven links and is not flattened to Copy as new plus View.
The filtered Action needed card for GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P shows 'Copy as new' and 'View'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 already judged this difference on the dashboard card, which moves with the dashboard to the INS front door, so the drill-down cards keep their status-driven links. The prototype claim is not overruled: it still backs the category filter on the Action needed list.

conflicts.about: Whether the drill-downs apply the search and sort the trader picks, when DR2.1 only preselects them.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
On the actions and inspection pages the search text and sort are not applied: the notifications show in the same order whatever is searched or sorted.
Today's search is trimmed, passed to ins-backend and applied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a search and sort over real data is behaviour the seeded prototype cannot express, so the real drill-downs apply both. The prototype's inert search is overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether the home and drill-downs use DR2.1's custom glance-card and intro styling or stay within GOV.UK Frontend components as today's dashboard does.

positions.says: The dashboard layout is custom app-overall-dashboard and glance-card markup, not a GOV.UK Frontend component.
The dashboard is built entirely from GOV.UK Frontend components, with no custom component in main.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks today's front door and no DR1 judgement or real constraint overrides it, so DR2.1's styling is built.

conflicts.about: Whether the drill-down 'Sort by:' select offers DR2.1's 'Select one' unsorted state.

positions.says: inc-031 rejected: the dashboard stays always sorted and no unsorted state is added.
The drill-down's 'Sort by:' select offers 'Select one', 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date'.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 already judged this difference on the dashboard, so the drill-downs are always sorted, 'Newest first' by default, with no 'Select one'. The prototype claim is not overruled: it still backs the search form and the three sort orders.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's 'At a glance' band (Alerts, Errors, Messages) or DR2.1's per-category glance cards summarise the home.

positions.says: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements.
Each category section has an 'Action needed' card and a 'Status updates' card.
DR1 shows an 'At a glance' section with Alerts, Errors and Messages cards (inc-014, blocked).

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: DR1's band is the earlier design, not a judgement, so DR2.1's per-category cards are built and DR1's band is overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether /dashboard redirects to the home (or, with a query, to the live animals list) as Design Release 2.1 does.

positions.says: req-1016 and inc-128's /dashboard redirect are dropped, and the redirect is struck from c-159 too.
Going to /dashboard with no query redirects to the overall dashboard.
Going to /dashboard with a query redirects to the live animals dashboard, keeping the query.
GET /dashboard with no query returns a 302 to the overall dashboard.
GET /dashboard?tab=drafts returns a 302 to the live-animals dashboard, keeping the query.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October ruling ranks first: the /dashboard redirect is a prototype URL, and the prototype never decides URL paths, so it is not built (req-1016 is out of scope).

conflicts.about: Whether the home's and drill-downs' links take Design Release 2.1's literal paths and ?category= query (/live-animals, /germinal-products, /actions?category=...) or go to the right pages by the INS service's own paths and parameter names.

positions.says: For req-972 and req-987, the View dashboard and Back links point wherever the list lives.
The prototype never decides URL paths, query parameter or form field names.
Acceptance criteria assert pages, headings and destinations, not literal paths or query strings.
The live animals 'View tasks' link goes to /actions?category=live-animals.
The germinal products card's 'View dashboard' link goes to /germinal-products.
A category-filtered drill-down's search form carries the category as a hidden field so a search stays within that category.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: each link goes to the page Design Release 2.1 shows (the category's own notification list in its own frontend, which for live animals and germinal products is the set root in the animals frontend and for plants the plants frontend's list; the drill-down showing only that category; the home), by each service's own paths and parameter names; the drill-downs' own paths /actions, /changes and /inspection are acceptable as new pages with no real path shape to follow. The prototype claims are not overruled: they still back each link's label and destination page.

conflicts.about: Where the category notification lists that the home's 'View dashboard' links and the drill-downs' Back links point to live: moved to the INS front door, or kept in each set's own frontend.

positions.says: inc-129 and c-159 are kept because Rhys's DR1 judgement moves the dashboard to the INS front door.
There is no backend list filter by category; each set's root redirects to its INS list.
The performance suite joins inc-129 because the live-animals set root stops rendering the notification list.
The dashboard and address book are temporary in the animals frontend and move to trade-imports-ins-frontend.
Keeping the live animals list in the animals frontend replaces, for this programme, the move to the INS frontend kept from DR1.
With the list staying in the animals frontend, each set's root renders its own list, replacing 'each set's root redirects to its INS list'.
The reframed list stays at the live-animals set root, and the k6 suite's list request does not move.
The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend and is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme.
This programme no longer builds the INS notification lists the overall home's category sections linked to; the lists stay in each set's own frontend.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October templates and afternoon rulings rank above the morning ruling: each category's notification list stays in its own frontend (live animals and germinal products at their set roots in the animals frontend, plants in the plants frontend), so the home's 'View dashboard' links and the drill-downs' Back links point there, and the k6 suite's visit to the live-animals set root does not move. The morning ruling's move to the INS front door, the redirect from each set root to an INS list and the performance suite's reason for joining that move are overruled. DR1's judgement is not overruled: it still backs hosting the overall home and the address book in the INS front door.

conflicts.about: Whether the INS home's Germinal products section is built in this programme.

positions.says: The INS home's germinal section, the germinal list and the germinal cards are built and no longer blocked.
inc-145, the germinal section on the INS home, is summary information and blocked.
The INS germinal list's 'Create new' and the INS home's germinal section leave this programme with the INS home.
The type question's Germinal option stays the way into a germinal notification.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: the INS home's germinal section waits with the rest of the overall home's summary information (req-979, blocked), and the type question's Germinal option is the way into a germinal notification. The morning ruling's claim is overruled; the germinal list and cards it also names are now carried by the afternoon ruling as the germinal set's own copy of the reframed list in the animals frontend, another area's work.
